supporting_observations.claim: At 14:11:07 UTC, WS-LMARTINS-01 connected through the proxy to updates.pixelforge-suite.co, using a process at C:\Users\leo.martins\AppData\Roaming\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe.

The observed updater path and hostname differ from the inventory's approved PixelForge updater path and updates.pixelforge-suite.com domain; this supports a masquerading or typo-squatting interpretation.

Several proxy HTTP connections from the workstation in the alert window have similar byte counts and occur at roughly five-minute intervals, including records around 13:45, 13:50, 13:54, 14:00, 14:06, and 14:11 UTC.
At 14:11:07 UTC, the proxy tunnel and workstation network events associate the outbound connection with the AppData PixelForge updater, rather than merely showing an unrelated browser connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records do not identify the process responsible for most of the earlier periodic proxy connections; the direct process-to-connection association is present for the 14:11:07 connection.
The proxy records show CONNECT hostnames and tunnel byte counts, not the encrypted HTTPS contents.
The supplied records do not include the updater's file hash, signature status, origin, or execution history.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish what data, if any, was sent or received inside the HTTPS tunnels.
The evidence does not establish whether the updater binary is malicious, signed, or part of an authorized installation.
The evidence does not establish successful compromise, persistence, or impact on the workstation.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze the AppData\Roaming\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe binary, including its hash, signature, creation and modification times, and origin.
Retrieve proxy and endpoint process-attribution records for each periodic connection in the alert window to determine whether they share the same process and destination.
Review DNS, TLS certificate or inspection telemetry, and proxy reputation data for updates.pixelforge-suite.co.
Examine endpoint execution, file-write, persistence, and security-product telemetry for related activity.
